The following diagnostic notes describe the behavior observed in the staging environment. The application starts successfully and answers the basic health check, but requests routed through the reverse proxy occasionally lose their session. Direct requests from the internal network do not reproduce the problem. This difference suggests that we should inspect the forwarded headers before changing application-level authentication settings.

The command examples below are provided for comparison with your existing configuration. Do not paste them into production without replacing the demonstration host names and checking the service names used by your installation. The output contains literal braces and angle brackets because it illustrates a template rather than a complete configuration file. Those characters are part of the example and should remain unchanged.

We need a short capture from the period immediately before and after a failed sign-in. A full-day archive is difficult to correlate and may contain unrelated information. Please include the request identifier returned to the browser and the matching entry from the proxy access log. If the request identifier is absent, record that fact explicitly rather than inventing a value to fill the field.

The exception message contains a function name that resembles ordinary English. It is still an identifier used by the application, and searching for a translated version will not find the relevant code. Please copy the exact identifier into the diagnostic record. The surrounding explanation can be written in your preferred language, but commands, paths, environment variable names, and error codes need to remain as they appeared.

After testing the header adjustment, repeat the same request from the original browser session and from a new session. A successful test with only the new session does not establish that existing sessions recovered. If the results differ, retain both observations in the report and record which test was performed first. This will help us distinguish a configuration effect from a session that simply expired during the investigation.

Once the staging result is stable, we can prepare a small production change with an explicit rollback step. Please avoid making unrelated cleanup changes in the same deployment. Even harmless formatting changes can make the final configuration diff harder to review. The change request should show the exact lines being modified and name the person responsible for checking delivery and background processing afterwards.

# Literal examples for the diagnostic record
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://demo@db.example.com/support
curl --retry 3 -H 'X-Request-ID: REQ-8f4a' https://example.com/health
getUserById(user_id) -> HTTP_429
{"retry": 3, "path": "C:\logs\app.txt", "template": "<tag>"}

Our recommendation is to deploy the configuration adjustment separately from the scheduled application upgrade. Combining both changes would make it difficult to determine which one affected the result. After the adjustment, allow the monitoring checks to complete and ask the service desk to confirm that normal work can continue. The upgrade can then proceed under its existing change approval, with its own rollback decision.

For the rollback, restore the exported configuration and restart only the component named in the change record. Do not restore the entire database: that would remove requests received since the backup and create a separate recovery problem. If the targeted restart does not restore service, stop the procedure and contact the on-call engineer with the recorded timestamps and the latest health-check output.

The monitoring dashboard can briefly show older results after the service has recovered. Please compare the timestamp of each check before treating a red indicator as a new failure. We are interested in checks performed after the restart, especially the request delivery test and the background processing test. A screenshot that includes the timestamp is more useful than a cropped image containing only the status icon.

We can confirm the state of a specific message more reliably than making a general statement about the whole queue.

There is one remaining question about the shared mailbox. We need to know whether another application reads messages from the same folder and moves them after processing. This can make a message disappear between two polling attempts even when both applications are operating correctly. Please ask the mailbox owner to describe the other integrations, including any rules that move messages into an archive or a project folder.
